note_tweet.text:
Lately I've seen a lot of people hitting their Grok bot limits, so here's the AI workflow I actually use day to day.

Short version: almost every task goes through Grok bot, split into separate bots by role. Grok bot sorts the task itself, then decides whether to do it or hand it off to an Orca session.

Light task, not many tokens? Grok bot just does it.

Long-running or token-heavy task? Grok bot passes it to Orca. For example:
- Fix a bug in my app
- Build a new web/mobile app
- Go research ideas, then bring them back to evaluate locally
- etc.

Orca is already great at managing AI agents. It takes tasks from Grok bot through the Orca CLI, then routes each one to the right Model + Agent pair.

Why this setup? Grok bot's strength is that it's easy to reach and easy to hand work to. Way easier than opening Orca Mobile and doing it myself.
And one command to Grok bot can fan out to multiple Orca sessions.

So Grok bot is just the coordinator. It handles light stuff: a bit of research, finding my ID card photo in Google Photos, digging up an email, putting something on my calendar. It never does the heavy lifting itself.

That's it. Grok bot won't hit limits easily. Last week I even gave it a few extra jobs because I had quota left, and still ended at around 8x%.

Want the technical picture? Here's all my gear and settings.

At home:

DGX Spark
- TensorFold running Qwen3.8-Flash-Next NVFP4 (switching to hypnos for good in a few days)
- 24/7 services via herdr sessions
- ComfyUI + Minimax H3
- Tailscale

The Spark does nothing but serve local models. Its memory is too precious for anything else.

Asus ROG Ally + XG Mobile RTX 4090
- ComfyUI + Qwen Image 2.1
- Tailscale

This one is purely for image generation.

Alienware (RTX 3070), 64GB RAM
- Running Omarchy instead of Windows for 2+ months now. Stable, light, and way better for agent work than Windows.
- Orca, the core of this whole setup
- Grok bot, my assistant taking tasks from me
- Thonburian Whisper medium + Ollama for speech-to-text, since I give more and more tasks by voice
- DeepSeek Harness for building small, specialized harnesses
- All 24/7 services run in Orca sessions, so I can manage them from anywhere
- Tailscale

The Alienware is the main machine, the heart of this workflow. On 24/7. I picked it for the RAM and the strong cooling fans.

Away from home, this is how I send tasks:

Main phone: Z Fold 8
- Orca Mobile to control Orca at home when I need to
- Grok bot, my main way to hand off tasks
- Omalauncher to try out ideas: build and run them on Arch Linux right on the phone
- ap-7 field recorder: when an idea hits, I record it and send it to Thonburian Whisper at home, which transcribes it, summarizes it and turns it into a mindmap
- Tailscale

My iPhone, iPad and MacBook have a similar setup to the Fold, but honestly I barely use them lol

Subscriptions I pay for right now:
- Claude $100 (mostly Sonnet 5.5)
- OpenCode Go $10 (mostly DeepSeek V4.1 Flash)
- X Premium+ $3x (for Grok bot)

Result: I almost never max out any of them, and work still runs smoothly every day.

"Can Hermes Agent replace Grok bot?" Technically, yes.
But after using Hermes for a while, I spent more time fixing Hermes than getting work out of it, so I stopped. If you're already fluent with it, I think it works just as well.

OpenAI Dots? Haven't tried it. Unsubbed a long time ago lol

Claude Duet? I use it, and I think it could replace Grok bot. But I'd rather save those tokens for heavier work. Better value.

"Why Orca? Can't you use T3 Code?" In principle, yes. But T3 Code crashed on me way too often, so I went back to Orca. And Orca's Chat Mode is now just as good as T3 Code's.

How do you set up your workflow? Share it below.

Hope this helps a little. Good luck!

Claude Duet 还在排队，GitHub 上已经有人做了免费开源版：6.7k 星，但它不是官方的，先看清能干什么
建议收藏。读完你能判断：这个开源版值不值得现在就装，以及第一次打开该点哪几步。
这是 GitHub 项目 Anil-matcha/open-duet 的 README（项目首页说明）写的，标题是《Open Duet》，不是 Anthropic 出的。先把结论放前面：它自称是 Claude Duet、OpenAI Dots、Meta Muse 等的开源、可自托管替代品，但官方 Claude Duet 眼下仍是美国 Pro/Max/Ultra 候补，两者是两个东西。
我查到的硬数字：项目页显示 6.7k 星、853 个 fork、554 次提交，协议 Apache-2.0。最近两天，英文圈好几条推荐帖都过了 500 赞，其中一条 1,043 赞。
先说清词。
引擎（engine），就是真正干活的那个 AI，比如 Claude Code、Codex CLI、Gemini CLI、Cursor，或者你自己的 API。Open Duet 本身不带模型，也不带订阅，你得自己带。
带头的智能体（lead agent），就是接你需求、拆成小任务、分给别的智能体的那一个。官方写明：带头的必须用 Claude 或 Codex。
例行任务（routine），就是定时、被网页钩子触发或手动跑的任务，跑完要你过目，它自己不会批准任何动作。
先把话说全：
官方 README 自己写了：项目早期、变化快，自托管服务器是实验性的，只给一个主人用，不是多人组织用的。
桌面安装包是实验性的、没签名，平台验证有限。
手机端只有源码，只在安卓模拟器试过，没在 iOS 或真机上试过，也没有推送通知。
连 Gmail、日历这类应用要走 Composio，而且只测过假的 Composio 服务，没测过真服务。
它还有一个单独运营的托管版 Suparagent，月费 15 美元、49 美元、99 美元三档，和开源核心是两回事。
一、它能做什么
官方列了这些：给智能体起名字、定岗位、选引擎、分工作区、配记忆；带头的把活拆给专家；定时跑例行任务；三种自由度，Ask first、Accept edits、Plan only；Today 页集中显示待批准的事；任务看板和日历；可复用的技能和模板。
二、第一步：装之前先准备
需要 Node.js 22 或更新、uv，以及电脑上至少一个引擎。用命令行引擎的话，先装好并登录，再打开 Open Duet。
三、第二步：照官方命令启动
git clone https://t.co/0uozNb8ZqP
cd open-duet/desktop
npm run app
首次启动选引擎、工作区和审批模式。
四、第三步：建第一个智能体
进 Settings → Engines，确认引擎显示就绪。新建智能体，写名字、一句话职责、工作区。开聊时选 Ask first，需要审批的动作它会先停下问你。
五、第四步：官方示例，每周项目简报
建一个带头的，再建研究员和编辑两个专家，给同一个项目工作区，带头的引擎选 Claude 或 Codex。让带头的根据文件夹里的笔记和报告做简报。它会拆活、分给专家，在各自对话里跑，再回来汇总。流程顺了，就把它变成每周例行任务，每次跑完你过目。
常见坑 3 条：一，它没有模型，没有引擎就是空壳。二，模型用量记在你自己的引擎账号上，官方说可能花钱，不是装了就免费。三，它是第三方项目，运行前请自己看一眼代码和权限，别把重要密钥随手交出去。
原文链接：https://t.co/3xDhab6ncC
原文：Anil-matcha/open-duet README（由 S1哥 编译）
S1哥观点
这条最值得看的，是官方 Claude Duet 还在候补，开源版已经 6.7k 星。说明大家要的不是某家的 App，而是“一队有名字有记忆、动手前先问我”的 AI 同事这个形态。
真正的信号是：它自己都写了“早期、变化快、部分功能是实验性的”，所以眼下适合拿来试玩学概念，不适合马上托付重要数据。就像试驾样车，能感受方向，别拉全家出远门。
评论区说一下，你想先让它的哪个智能体干活：研究员还是编辑？你卡在第几步？同系列前几篇在我主页。
这是 Claude Duet 更新速递，关注 @swordBluesy。
今天送：Open Duet 上手速查包，评论区第一条直接拿。

This compares cost for my workload, not model quality or equivalent capabilities.

One last thing, @elonmusk:

Bundling Grok, Grok Bot, Cursor, a persistent cloud computer and full X Premium+ benefits into The @X Subscription was a smart move.

For my usage, the combined package is more compelling than token pricing alone.

Are the labs holding the models back for internal use? Or was September just an outlier?

Even Elon says Grok 4.8 isn't being built for benchmarks. It's meant to be "incredibly useful". SpaceX is shipping over 100 changes a week now for Grok Bot.

Claude Duet and ChatGPT dots look like they were rushed out to keep up.

Is the agent market the real frontier?

note_tweet.text:
I built a shopping app called Sweetcouch. It reached 10 million users, was backed by Sequoia, and was named among the Best iPhone Shopping Apps of 2016.

Then AI arrived, and honestly, we were clueless.

How do you put AI inside a consumer product? The easy answer is to bolt a chatbot onto the existing app. It’s a patchwork, and we decided to avoid any such temptation.

We decided to educate us on generative AI and spent a year learning it. Here’s what we discovered. Software follows rules we write into it. An AI-native product puts intelligence at the centre. AI-enabled is easy. AI-native meant rethinking shopping from scratch. It took us a year just to unlearn how we used to build.

A second realisation.
Most consumer AI and personal agents, like Meta Muse, OpenAI Dots, Instinct and Grok bots, are built to save you time. But shopping isn’t a chore for most women. It’s how they explore, unwind and express themselves.

So why would AI take that joy away? It should make it richer.

That’s why we built THINGS: a styling team of five AI experts.
→ Inspector finds niche shops and vets them
→ Editor curates your looks every morning and tells you why they suit you
→ ME shows any look on you before you buy
→ Ego teaches you what works and finds what your wardrobe is missing
→ Accountant hunts the best prices and flags shipping and return fine print

You don’t see the agents. You just enjoy their work.

THINGS is free to start. We’re rolling out in India first, then globally.

#ConsumerAI #AIAgents #FashionTech #GenAI #PersonalAgents
